# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_001_page_001.jpg

---

1:1 Love righteousness, you who are judges of the earth; think upon the Lord in goodness, and seek him with sincerity of heart.

1:2 For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who do not distrust him.

1:3 For perverse thoughts separate one from God, and when his power is tested, it convicts the foolish.

1:4 For wisdom will not enter a deceitful soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sin.

1:5 For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, will withdraw from senseless thoughts, and will be rebuked when unrighteousness approaches.

1:6 For wisdom is a kindly spirit, yet she will not acquit the blasphemer of his words; because God is witness of his inmost being, a true observer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

1:7 Because the spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together knows every voice.

1:8 Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will go undetected, nor will justice, when it brings judgment, pass him by.

1:9 For inquiry will be made into the counsels of the ungodly, and a report of his words will come before the Lord as proof of his lawless deeds.

1:10 Because an attentive ear hears all things, and the noise of complaints is not hidden.

1:11 Therefore beware of worthless complaining, and keep your tongue from slander; for no secret word is without consequence, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.

1:12 Do not invite death by the error of your life, nor bring destruction upon yourselves by the work of your hands.

1:13 For God did not make death, and he takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living.

1:14 For he created all things so that they might have being; and the generative forces of the world are life-giving, and there is no destructive venom in them, nor is the dominion of Hades on earth.

1:15 For righteousness is immortal.

1:16 But it is the ungodly who by their hands and words have summoned death; counting it as a friend, they have wasted away, and they have made a covenant with it, because they deserve to belong to its company.

---

*LOGOS notes: "Sincerity of heart" (haplotēti kardias) captures both the simplicity and integrity of intent. "Kindly spirit" renders philanthrōpon pneuma — literally "humanity-loving spirit." Verse 14's "life-giving" renders hygieines — wholesome/healthy. Verse 15 is placed as an independent aphorism, as the Greek warrants.*
